sections.h2: What does the Sampson County Register of Deeds record?
sections.html:
The Sampson County Register of Deeds is the county's official custodian of real estate records, and it keeps a permanent record of ownership and transfers. The county says the office records deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names, powers of attorney and other real estate papers.

The same office handles birth, death and marriage certificates, issues marriage licenses, records military discharges and keeps notary public commission records. Most sellers deal only with the land records side, usually through a closing attorney who files the deed after signing.

The county site links to online access for the Register of Deeds records, so you can look up your own deed and any deed of trust before a buyer's title company does. Begin there to find the book and page of the instrument that put you on title. A seller who inherited the house can often trace the path of ownership back through each recorded deed to confirm every name on the chain is correct.

sections.h2: Can the Sampson County office help me prepare a deed?
sections.html:
No. The county states that the office acts as a recording office only, and North Carolina law bars the register of deeds and staff from practicing law. Staff cannot supply legal forms, explain how to fill them out, or advise on the legal effect of a filed instrument.

That limit shapes how a Sampson County sale works in practice. A few jobs belong to others:

  • An attorney drafts the deed and answers questions about its wording.
  • A title company or closing attorney checks the chain of title and arranges payoffs.
  • The register of deeds checks the filing against recording requirements, collects the fee and tax, and indexes the instrument.

If you are selling a house that came to you through a family arrangement, get an attorney's advice first, because the recorder cannot repair a deed that was written wrong.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed transfer tax in a Sampson County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. State law puts an excise tax on each deed that conveys an interest in real property at $1.00 for each $500 of the price or value, and the transferor pays the register of deeds in the county where the land lies before the deed is recorded (G.S. 105-228.30).

The tax revenue is shared. Half goes to the Sampson County general fund and the other half goes to the state, less refunds and an allowance. For a parcel that spans two counties, the tax is paid in the county holding the greater value.

Have your closing attorney list the excise tax as a separate line on the settlement statement. Seeing it in advance means you will know your net proceeds before you sign.

sections.h2: How much does recording cost in Sampson County?
sections.html:
The register of deeds charges the uniform statewide fees in G.S. 161-10, which the statute describes as complete and exclusive.

Statewide recording fees that apply in Sampson County
ItemPrinted figureSource
Instrument in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 for each added pageG.S. 161-10
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for the first 35 pages, plus $4.00 for each added pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo feeG.S. 161-10
Plat$21.00 per sheetG.S. 161-10
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Nonstandard document add-on$25.00G.S. 161-10
Each added instrument in one document$10.00G.S. 161-10

Fees are collected before the instrument is filed. If you plan to record several papers together, such as a deed and a plat, ask for the total ahead of time.

sections.h2: Why does the time a deed is recorded matter in Sampson County?
sections.html:
Recording fixes priority. A deed, option, right of first refusal, or lease of more than three years does not bind lien creditors or later buyers who paid value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and rank follows the order of registration (G.S. 47-18).

On a sale, your buyer's deed and the buyer's lender's deed of trust are normally filed right after closing. On your side, the payoff of your old loan should be followed by a recorded satisfaction, which carries no fee. An old deed of trust that never gets cancelled can show up on a later title search and slow another sale.

Ask the register of deeds for a certified copy of the recorded deed when the sale is done. The statutory fee is $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.

sections.h2: What happens with unpaid taxes or a tax foreclosure on a Sampson County parcel?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax is a lien on the parcel from the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs attach at the same time (G.S. 105-355). The county can enforce it by an action like a mortgage foreclosure in the county where the land lies (G.S. 105-374).

  • The sale is a public auction to the highest bidder at the courthouse door.
  • The commissioner may require a deposit of up to 20 percent of the bid.
  • Exceptions or an increased bid can be filed within 10 days after the report of sale.
  • Before confirmation, a person redeeming pays all taxes plus penalties, interest and costs.

Sampson County property tax bills are covered on a separate page, and the tax office can give a payoff figure for any parcel.

sections.h2: What other situations affect recording on an inherited or contract-for-deed Sampson County house?
sections.html:
Estates and installment sales add paperwork. For a small estate of personal property worth $20,000 or less after liens, an heir may use an affidavit under G.S. 28A-25-1 after waiting 30 days from death, filed with the clerk of superior court where the decedent lived.

A contract for deed on a one to four family home must be recorded, or a memorandum of it, by the seller within five business days, and the buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing (Chapter 47H). Forfeiture needs a written notice with a cure date at least 30 days after service.

If a foreclosure sale draws an upset bid, the bid must exceed the last one by at least 5 percent and by at least $750, and it is due by close of business on the tenth day after the report (G.S. 45-21.27). Each upset bid restarts the ten days.

faqs.q: Can the Sampson County register of deeds give me legal advice about a deed?
faqs.a: No. The county says the office is a recording office only and that staff may not practice law, supply legal forms or explain how to fill them out. Hire an attorney for drafting questions.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax rate in Sampson County?
faqs.a: State law sets it at $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or value, or fractional part. The seller pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, and the county and state split the money.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Sampson County?
faqs.a: The state fee is $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each added page. A deed of trust costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 per added page. Satisfactions are free.

faqs.q: What else does the Sampson County Register of Deeds handle besides land records?
faqs.a: It also issues birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage licenses, records military discharges, and keeps notary commission records, according to the county site.

faqs.q: Does recording a deed protect the buyer?
faqs.a: Yes, in the way the statute describes. A conveyance is valid against lien creditors and later buyers for value only from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies, so prompt filing secures the buyer's place in line.
